title: Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations
main_claim: For an invertible mixing transformation T, every n>=2 and bounded f_1..f_n, (1/N) sum_{k<=N} prod_j f_j(T^{jk}x) converges a.e. to prod_j int f_j, along all N; no standardness or mixing rate needed.

issues.description: The result is conditional on companion papers that are not reproduced here. MixingCompanion Thm 1.1 claims that mixing implies mixing of all orders, which is Rokhlin's problem, open since 1949. SlopesCompanion Prop 3.5/Lemma 3.9 claims pointwise triple convergence at distinct slopes on arbitrary systems, also a famous open problem. FourfoldCompanion Prop 2.2 and Thm 4.1 supply the nonergodic structure theory. Within this paper the reduction to these inputs is complete, but the main theorem is only as strong as they are.
issues.evidence: Introduction: 'These companion proofs are not reproduced here'. Thm 2.1 is used in channel closure (mixing of all orders). Lemma 2.5 (triple convergence) is used for the |J|<=3 marginals, which give k>=4.

issues.description: The paper asserts that the supremum of the energy over all standard flow extensions can be taken over a set, via coding standard spaces, actions and factor maps on fixed standard spaces. This is only sketched. It is standard (Austin's sated extensions) but not written out.
issues.evidence: 'It can be taken over a set: standard Borel spaces, their probability laws, Borel actions, and factor maps admit codes on fixed standard spaces.'

coverage: Read all sections (intro, inputs, selected, channels, correlations, square, packing appendix). Verified: (1) Lemma 2.4 relative norm VdC induction. (2) Lemma 2.5 smooth-to-sharp transference with a rational grid. (3) Selector witness: phase identity Psi=alpha(u)beta(s) via v2-v1=s and 2v1-v2=u; the supports guarantee u+is<1 so there is no roof crossing. (4) Selected-law existence, invariance with error 2|t0|2^-a, functoriality and inverse limits. (5) Small conditional law: rwm conditional product plus distal parameter joining, then relative disjointness. (6) Channel conditioning (V lies in W_Y; spatial factor at time h is mixing x id, hence rwm). (7) Channel closure: proper-group case via multiple mixing and Birkhoff for T^{hb}; density bounds 0<=p rho<=1 and ||p rho||_2<=sqrt p; Cauchy-Schwarz for the projected part using the unchanged two-group marginals; residual tr(AB)<=||A|| tr B<=m^2/d_m; dyadic sum with d_m^{-1}=O(k^{-3/2}); bounded-degree graph from the separation inequalities. (8) Appendix: Gaussian moment recursion and AM-GM trace bound, q~log d choice, spectral splitting at sqrt d, covering counts, cluster bound (1+L)/|A|+eta, Sudakov-Fernique with variance eps^2/128 vs separation eps/8, and the o(m) exponent (log m)^{3/4}loglog m. (9) Minimum support k>=4; minimum-product lemma; r<k from Cor 4.4. (10) Regrouped channel: the all-centered term is killed by maximality of r; the surjection tau ensures fewer than k slots for proper H. (11) Saturation energy monotonicity argument. (12) Square: column law lambda_Y by functoriality; row law via one-slot marginal; row-column identity from saturation at datum indices 0 and b; derived law(slot b | e)=m_{Y,kappa(e)}. (13) Parameter conditional independence via change of variable z'=S^{bt}z with kappa-measurability. (14) R_*beta_w=alpha_w; fibre tower; independent-copy orthogonality argument. (15) Final role count: k slots and r+1 output roles, with centeredness checked.
